newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Tuesday drop.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Tuesday drop.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Wednesday, extending yesterday's decline on falling cash prices and the two units at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) near full output.
"It still feels weak out there. Daily prices are still much lower than futures," a Houston futures trader said.

In over-the-counter business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $33.55-33.65 a megawatt hour (MWh) down more than a dollar from Tuesday's settlement at $33.80, and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $20.00-20.50 against yesterday's close at $20.46.
Day-ahead power prices for Thursday at PV were discussed at $26.50-28.00 a MWh, while those at COB was quoted near $17.00 in early activity, market sources said.

The 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2 and 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3, in San Clemente, California, were operating at 97 percent and 82 percent power, respectively as of early Wednesday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
Analysts said they expect chart support for August PV in the $32.00 area and August COB near the $18.00 level.
The operator Southern California Edison Co said both SONGS units would resume full output before the end of the week.
Forecasters expected seasonal summer weather across most of the West through next week.

Coastal cities from Seattle to Los Angeles were forecast to see readings in the 70s Fahrenheit, while interior centers in Southwest like Phoenix and Las Vegas were called to hit the 100 degree mark later this week.
The Western Systems Coordinating Council was tentatively set to vote this week on raising the capacity of the Pacific Intertie transmission system to 6,900 MW from 6,300 MW.
Increased power flow from the hydroelectric projects in the Pacific Northwest to southern California would take effect August 1.
